card.title: Rotate an Array to the Right

a1.cap: Rotate nums to the right by k steps in place: each value moves k positions right, wrapping around to the front. Use O(1) extra memory.
a1.say: Rotate nums to the right by k steps in place: each value moves k positions right, wrapping around to the front. Use O of one extra memory.

lines: Rotate nums to the right by k steps in place: each value moves k positions right, wrapping around to the front. Use O(1) extra memory.

a1.cap: For example, with nums = [1,2,3,4,5,6,7], k = 3, the answer is [5,6,7,1,2,3,4].
a1.say: For example, with nums equals 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, k equals 3, the answer is 5, 6, 7, 1, 2, 3, 4.

a1.cap: Reverse the whole array, then reverse the first k values, then reverse the rest. Each reversal is a classic two-pointer swap from both ends.
The first reversal moves the last k values to the front (backwards); the next two put each part back in the right order.
Let's walk through it with nums = [1,2,3,4,5], k = 2.
a1.say: Let's walk through it with nums equals 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, k equals 2.

a1.cap: Time complexity is O(n) and extra space is O(1).
a1.say: Time complexity is O of n and extra space is O of one.

a1.cap: That's the Reverse Three Times approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
